request.spec:
A person may have an approver: a user name on the row (an entry and a button; APPROVER_SET
name=<name> user=<user>). That user may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward
may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may have an approver: a user name on the row (an entry and a button; APPROVER_SET
name=<name> user=<user>). That user may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward
may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person can now have an approver, who can approve or reject that person's PENDING claims the same way a steward can. All 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`, including on a rerun of the final code.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration `V113__person_approver.sql` adds an `approver` column to `person`. The `Person` entity has the field, and copying a sheet (`clonedTo`) carries it over.
- **Server:**
  - A new endpoint, `POST /{personId}/approver`, sets the approver. A blank value clears it.
  - Each change writes an `APPROVER_SET sheet=… by=… name=<person> user=<approver>` record to the audit file.
  - The person's details sent to the screen now include the approver.
  - The approve/reject permission check in `ClaimService` (`lockPending`) now accepts a steward or the person's approver. The existing rule still applies: whoever opened or last edited a claim cannot approve it.
- **Front end:** each person's row shows the approver (`person-approver`) and has an input and button to set it (`person-approver-input`, `person-approver-save`). A failure shows in `person-error`. I also reworded the approve/reject refusal messages to mention the approver.

**Decisions to check:**
- **Who can set an approver:** anyone signed in can, because the request doesn't restrict it and the test never expects a refusal. If only stewards should, it's a one-line role check in `PersonService.setApprover`.
- **No name check:** any typed name is accepted, without checking it's a user of the sheet.
- **Transfers and history:** moving a person to another sheet doesn't take the approver with them. Approver changes also aren't kept in the person's revision history, so undoing an edit leaves the approver as it is.
